summary: Child workflow cancellation on Python 3.11+ emits spurious ERROR log warnings and sends duplicate RequestCancelExternalWorkflow commands due to missing task.uncancel() call in run_child() after catching CancelledError.
userImpact: Users calling handle.cancel() on child workflows see spurious ERROR log messages and multiple duplicate cancellation commands sent to the server on Python 3.11+.
rootCause: run_child() in _workflow_instance.py catches CancelledError without calling task.uncancel(), leaving Python 3.11+'s cancellation counter at 1, causing CancelledError to be re-thrown on subsequent awaits.
proposedFix: Call task.uncancel() after catching CancelledError to clear the cancellation counter, allowing the next await to block normally instead of immediately re-raising CancelledError.
workaround: Install a logging.Filter on 'temporalio.worker._workflow_instance' logger to suppress error records matching both 'ChildWorkflowError exception in shielded future' and 'Child Workflow execution cancelled'.
keyQuote: In Python 3.11, asyncio.Task introduced a cancellation counter. When task.cancel() is called and the coroutine catches CancelledError without calling task.uncancel(), the cancelling counter remains at 1.
